content.title: About
content.content: Green bell pepper is the unripe fruit of the Capsicum annuum plant. It has a crisp texture, mildly bitter flavor, and bright green color. The pepper is eaten raw and also used in cooking for sautéing, roasting, and stewing.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Green peppers are simply unripe fruits that turn red, yellow or orange as they mature.
They contain more vitamin C than many citrus fruits.
Bell peppers belong to the nightshade family, along with tomatoes and eggplants.
Green peppers feature in traditional dishes worldwide, such as Mexican chile relleno and Italian ratatouille.
There are over 50,000 varieties of sweet peppers, differing in shape, flavor and color.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system, aids collagen synthesis, and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Contains vitamin A and carotenoids
items.content: Beta‑carotene converts to vitamin A, which is essential for vision and skin health.

items.title: Low‑calorie source of fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium assists in fluid balance and supports proper heart function.

items.title: Provides folate
items.content: Folate is important for DNA synthesis and is especially beneficial during pregnancy.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to peppers, such as itching, swelling or hives.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Improperly washed peppers can retain pesticide residues; thorough rinsing is recommended before consumption.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Raw peppers can cause gas and stomach discomfort in sensitive people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Peppers can be eaten raw in salads, sliced into sticks for dipping, added to sandwiches and smoothies. In cooking they are often sautéed, roasted or stewed, which softens the flavor while preserving nutrients.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store green bell peppers in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, placed in a perforated bag. When kept properly they stay fresh for 1–2 weeks. Discard any peppers that become soft, develop spots, or emit an off‑odor.
